name: Minnesota
note: The mortician or other person in charge of disposition files the death record with the state registrar within five days and before disposition, collecting fact of death from the hospital or medical examiner and the cause from the certifier; no disposition permit issues until the fact-of-death record is filed. From the state record, the commissioner of health reports deceased adults monthly and electronically to the secretary of state, and county auditors must mark those voters deceased within 60 days. Certified copies are limited to a statutory list of relatives, fiduciaries and those with a property right, while the information in vital records is otherwise public. No state-law death feed to the driver licence, tax or Medicaid agencies was found; federal routes (SSA, LADMF) are in us-federal.

steps.title: Determination of death under accepted medical standards
steps.who: The attending practitioner; Minnesota's Uniform Determination of Death Act sets the criteria but does not name who may pronounce.
steps.summary: Death is irreversible cessation of circulatory and respiratory functions or of all brain functions, determined under generally accepted medical standards. The mortician later collects the fact of death from the hospital, nursing home, coroner or medical examiner.

steps.title: Report sudden, unnatural and listed deaths to the coroner or medical examiner
steps.who: Anyone with knowledge of the death; reportable deaths include unnatural, suspicious and unattended deaths, deaths in custody, deaths in emergency departments, and deaths of persons whose bodies are to be cremated.
steps.trigger: A death of a listed kind.
steps.summary: Twenty-four categories of death must be promptly reported to the coroner or medical examiner, who then supplies the cause of death. Cremation cases are among them, so cremations pass through the medical examiner.

steps.title: Certifier supplies cause of death to the registrar
steps.who: A physician present at death, who treated the decedent, or with direct knowledge and access to the record; or the coroner or medical examiner. The statute also names advanced practice registered nurses and physician assistants among those who file.
steps.trigger: Request from the state registrar or the person in charge of disposition.
steps.summary: The cause of death is entered by the certifier separately from the funeral director's fact-of-death and demographic filing; the registrar or the mortician contacts the physician to request it.

steps.title: Mortician files the death record with the state registrar
steps.who: The mortician, funeral director, or other person lawfully in charge of final disposition. Demographic data come from relatives, friends or records.

deadline.text: within five days after death and prior to final disposition

steps.summary: Every death is filed with the state registrar (not a local registrar) within five days and before disposition. The registrar may prescribe electronic submission. False statements are a misdemeanour.

steps.title: Disposition permit only after the fact-of-death record is filed
steps.who: Issued for burial, entombment, cremation, alkaline hydrolysis or natural reduction.
steps.summary: Registration gates disposition: no permit may be issued until the fact-of-death record is completed and filed with the state registrar.

steps.title: Certified death record to listed relatives and fiduciaries
steps.who: Child, spouse, parent, grandparent/grandchild, sibling, guardian or health care agent, personal representative or successor (by affidavit), trustee, a person showing a personal or property right, an attorney, or by court order. Issued by the state registrar or a local issuance office.
steps.summary: Certified copies are tiered: eligible applicants sign an attestation; a mortician may attest for eligible relatives within 180 days of death. The information in death records is otherwise public, so non-certified copies are not restricted.

steps.title: Certified record to any government agency that needs it
steps.who: Any local, state, tribal or federal agency for its authorised duties.
steps.summary: Government agencies may obtain certified death records on request; this is a pull, not a feed.

steps.title: Report of a non-resident's death to the state of residence
steps.who: The vital records office of the decedent's state of residence.
steps.trigger: Registration of a death of a resident of another state.
steps.summary: When a resident of another state dies in Minnesota, the state registrar sends a report of the death to that state.

steps.title: Commissioner of health reports deceased adults to the secretary of state monthly
steps.who: The commissioner of health, to the secretary of state; residents 18 or older.
steps.trigger: Deaths registered since the last report.
steps.summary: Under the Help America Vote Act provision, health sends name, address, date of birth and county monthly by electronic means; the secretary of state matches against the voter file and lists matches for each county auditor.

steps.title: County auditor marks matched voters deceased
steps.who: The secretary of state, to each county auditor.
steps.trigger: The secretary of state's list of registrants who have died.

deadline.text: within 60 days after receiving the list

steps.summary: The auditor must change those registrants' status to deceased in the statewide voter registration system within 60 days.

steps.title: Voter file also matched against SSA death data and other states' reports
steps.who: The secretary of state, using the Social Security Death Index and other states' vital records reports.
steps.trigger: Receipt of the external death data.
steps.summary: Deaths outside Minnesota's own registry reach the voter roll through SSA data and other states' vital records departments.

steps.title: Obituary or voter's statement for deaths outside the county
steps.who: Anyone supplying a printed obituary, or a registered Minnesota voter's signed statement, to the county auditor.
steps.trigger: Death of a voter outside the county.
steps.summary: The county auditor changes the voter's status to deceased on a printed obituary or a signed statement.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Five days after death and before final disposition, filed directly with the state registrar.

informantDuty.note: The mortician, funeral director or other person in charge of disposition files; relatives only supply demographic information.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of every certificate. Listed deaths, including every death where the body is to be cremated, must be reported to the coroner or medical examiner.

electronicRegistration.note: The registrar may prescribe electronic submission; no statute read makes electronic filing mandatory.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; the Office of Vital Records holds the death record and pushes it only to the bodies the statutes name.

governmentPropagation.note: Under state law registration automatically reaches the voter roll (health to secretary of state to county auditors) and the state of residence of non-residents; other agencies must request certified copies. No statutory death feed to driver licensing, revenue or Medicaid was found. Federal feeds are in us-federal.

certificateAccess.note: Vital records information is public by default; certified death records go only to listed relatives, fiduciaries, those with a personal or property right, attorneys and agencies.

gaps: privateSectorVerification is left to the us-federal layer (LADMF); no Minnesota-law route for banks or insurers to verify deaths was found beyond the 'personal or property right' ground for a certified copy (§ 144.225, subd. 7(a)(1)(xi)).
No statutory death notice to Driver and Vehicle Services was found in § 171.12 (read for 'death'/'deceased'); chapter 171 was not read in full.

No Minnesota-law death feed to the Department of Revenue or to DHS (Medical Assistance) was found; chapters 289A and 256B were not searched in full because the revisor's full-text search runs on www.leg.state.mn.us, which is not reachable.
Whether the state registrar's electronic death record (MR-EDRS) feeds SSA is not stated in the statutes or rules read; the federal side belongs in us-federal.
No statute or rule names who may pronounce death (e.g., registered nurses); only the determination-of-death criteria (§ 145.135) were found.
